svg.title: How a monk's year became the world's
svg.desc: A linear timeline from about 4 BC to 1614. Marks: the usual date of Herod the Great's death, about 4 BC; Dionysius Exiguus setting year one in 525; Bede spreading the count in 725 and 731; Charlemagne requiring computus in schools in 789; and Laurentius Suslyga and Johannes Kepler pinning down the error in 1605 to 1614.

text.font-family: 'Liberation Serif', 'Iowan Old Style', Palatino, Georgia, serif

svg.text: A linear scale, from about 4 BC to 1614. There is no year zero, so the span is 1,617 years.
